findings.summary: The test-host fixture doc still frames ArrTags' DataFolderPath as PluginsPath/ArrTags and the release blocker as open; canonical current-state surfaces were updated and are accurate.
findings.detail: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md (lines 149-156, unmodified by the task) states Jellyfin derives ArrTags' DataFolderPath as data/plugins/ArrTags and says 'the release blocker is recorded in PLANS.md', which now records it as resolved. The general derivation statement is still true of BasePlugin<T>, and the caution 'Do not leave ArrTags state under data/plugins/ArrTags' remains valid (an orphaned folder still triggers the collision, per ADR-014), so this is a minor staleness in a test-fixture doc rather than a contradiction. All canonical surfaces (PLANS.md, changelog, README, architecture, readiness, decisions) were updated consistently.
findings.recommended_action: Optional follow-up: refresh the test-host doc bullet to note the 7.7 relocation/ADR-014 when task 7.3-7.5 next touch the fixture.

findings.summary: The new OnUninstalling state-root deletion could not be exercised through the live host uninstall API; it is covered in-process and the live host limitation is documented.
findings.detail: DELETE /Plugins/40322d52-5680-449f-b33e-e01836ee2f46/0.1.0.0 returned HTTP 401 (RequiresElevation policy, StartupWizardCompleted=false), independently reproduced. The worker's live 'uninstall' therefore removed the folder manually, which does not invoke OnUninstalling and leaves the relocated state root. The explicit cleanup is covered by PluginStateLocationTests (completed drain deletes, incomplete drain retains) and the pre-existing drain facts; InstallationManager.UninstallPlugin -> OnUninstalling was confirmed by source inspection. This is the same pre-existing live limitation recorded for task 7.2.
findings.recommended_action: None required; retain the documented limitation for the remaining Phase 7 verifications.

findings.summary: An orphaned pre-release PluginsPath/ArrTags folder would still trigger the discovery collision until an operator deletes it once; ADR-014 documents this and V1 has no released installs.
findings.detail: The fix stops the plugin from creating PluginsPath/ArrTags, but if an unreleased developer install already left that folder, the live negative control showed discovery still deletes the versioned install and loads no plugin. ADR-014 and docs/implementation-readiness.md document the one-time operator deletion; released V1 installs never create the folder, so no migration is implemented (consistent with the no-released-installs constraint).
evidence: Live negative control: /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags + ArrTags_0.1.0.0 -> install folder deleted, 0 ArrTags loads
findings.recommended_action: None required for V1; keep the one-time-deletion note visible for any pre-release tester.

findings.summary: The live state record was written with production code via a probe, not by the running plugin, because the plugin performs no state I/O on startup with no configured providers or library items.
findings.detail: The plugin path derivation (DataFolderPath -> ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.CreateStateRepository root) is deterministic and unit-tested, and the probe constructed the real production Plugin. The live A/B still proves discovery safety. A live end-to-end state write by a running plugin remains a Phase 5/7 carry-forward unrelated to this task (no provider/library item available).
evidence: Live positive run: /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags state present, install folder survived restart
